requiredActions: In pa-fe-dev's src/cdk/metric-detail/MetricDetailMY.tsx, the sections[] switch currently wraps every section (including GAUGE and COMPARISON) in its own independent <div className="section">. For metricCode TPC/PTPC only, detect a GAUGE section immediately followed by a COMPARISON section and render both inside one shared card container instead of two separate ones (title from the gauge section's variant, per AC-P4-02-21). Every other section type keeps its own independent card, unchanged.

Add the breakpoint rules for this combined card only in src/dls-stub/dls.css, following the existing .shell breakpoint pattern (already at 768px/1024px, matching common/ux/tokens/breakpoint.tokens.json breakpoint.tablet/breakpoint.desktop): below breakpoint.desktop, stack the GaugeDonut content above a horizontal divider above the ComparisonCard content; at breakpoint.desktop and above, place them in a two-column grid (gauge left, comparison right) with a vertical divider. No raw colors/sizes outside dls.css.
No VM, BFF route, or fixture changes — GaugeSectionVM and ComparisonSectionVM are unchanged; this is a pure rendering/CSS change in MetricDetailMY.tsx and dls.css.

Add a Playwright e2e test named after AC-P4-02-21 covering both TPC's mobile/tablet viewport (single column, horizontal divider) and desktop viewport (two columns, vertical divider); assert the two sections share one card container (e.g. same parent test id/role) rather than two.
Do not extend this combined-card treatment to FYP or CASE_COUNT (same gauge.primary+comparison.primary pairing per the screen spec's §1 matrix) — the spec's open question on that scope is unresolved.

openQuestions: AC-P4-02-21 is evidenced only for TPC from three requester screenshots, not a Figma export or approved asset — tracked under the existing "Strict UX source approval is incomplete" screen blocker, not a new one.
Whether FYP/CASE_COUNT (same gauge.primary+comparison.primary pairing) should adopt the same combined-card grouping is unresolved (README OQ-26).

Whether the screenshots' donut-less gauge face redefines w.metric-detail.gauge's donut-270 variant is unresolved (README OQ-27) — the frontend must keep rendering the existing donut visualization inside the gauge column until this is answered.

Ownership of the breadcrumb and collapsing left nav rail shown in the screenshots (host app shell vs a future Insights screen-chrome package) is unresolved (README OQ-28) and out of scope for this handoff.
